data.title: Tesla Supplier Simwon America Files for IPO — Update
data.description:
By Josh Beckerman

Simwon America, which provides parts for Tesla, filed for an initial public offering.

The company expects to sell 1.5 million shares and expects stockholders to offer 1 million, with an expected price range of $18 to $22 each.

The Lathrop, Calif., company's indirect parent companies MS Autotech Co., Ltd. and Myoung Shin Industry Co., Ltd. are listed in Korea.

Simwon America is seeking a Nasdaq Global Market listing under symbol SWA.

The company focuses on "Body-in-White" components.

In the risk factor section of its IPO filing, Simwon America notes that "we currently derive substantially all of our revenue from Tesla." For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, sales to Tesla accounted for about 99.5% of total revenue.

For the year ended June 30, 2026, revenue was down 13% to $323.9 million as "growth in the electric vehicle market moderated compared to prior periods."

The company has a 277,208-square-foot assembly facility and 198,183-square-foot fabrication facility in Lathrop. It plans to use some IPO proceeds to buy a company on the East Coast to support expansion and for expansion initiatives targeting the Mexican and Canadian markets.

Write to Josh Beckerman at josh.beckerman@wsj.com

data.title: Visa set to continue gains for seven straight sessions; up nearly 2.5%
data.description:
Visa is set to extend its winning streak to seven consecutive sessions as the stock jumped nearly 2.5% during afternoon trading on Friday.

The company gained nearly 4.25% over the previous six sessions. Overall, the stock has risen more than 8% so far this year, compared with a nearly 13.5% gain for the broader S&P 500 Index.

Visa is up nearly 4% over the past month. The stock closed 0.8% higher on Thursday at $375.10.

Looking at Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating, Visa has a Hold rating, with a score of 3.43 out of 5. The company received an A+ for profitability and a B+ for momentum, while it received an F for valuation.

However, Wall Street analysts and Seeking Alpha analysts are bullish, rating the stock a Strong Buy and Buy, respectively.

Seeking Alpha analyst Cyn Research said, “I view Visa as one of the more attractive ways to benefit from AI, as it can monetize agentic commerce and internal productivity gains without having to win the much riskier parts of the AI trade.”

The analyst considered stablecoins more of an opportunity than a threat, as Visa builds infrastructure across multiple coins, chains, and tokenized payment formats.

Cyn Research added that value-added services remain a major growth driver, with third-quarter revenue up 33% YoY and several portfolios consistently growing above 20%.

“Q3’s weaker profit growth initially concerned me, but one-offs, restructuring effects, and Q4 guidance make me expect earnings growth to move back above revenue growth,” the analyst concluded.

Turning to the Wall Street analyst community, 36 out of 40 analysts rated Visa Buy or higher, while three analysts rated the stock Hold, and one recommended a Sell.

data.title: IBM Stocks Edge Higher Although Truist Questions AI Payoff Timing
data.description:
IBM, the enterprise-technology and hybrid-cloud company , received a Hold rating and $240 price target as Truist Securities began coverage, with shares up to $227.16 at 10:52 a.m. ET on October 9. That leaves roughly 5.7% upside to the analyst's target. A strong bounce. A restrained endorsement.

According to Truist's assessment, IBM has plenty working in its favor: mainframes, Red Hat, software that works across AI models and a sizable consulting business. The sticking point is timing. Customers are pouring money into computing infrastructure, but that does not automatically mean an immediate rush of orders for IBM's data tools, orchestration software or implementation services. Building capacity and putting it to profitable use are separate spending decisions.

The valuation snapshot puts shares 6.59% below the $243.18 GF Value estimate, suggesting a modest discount rather than a deep bargain. Investors may be warming to IBM after its post-earnings decline, but the next leg needs evidence. Watch software bookings, consulting signings and AI projects moving into production. IBM's opportunity is to help customers turn expensive computing capacity into useful business results. The test is how quickly that opportunity becomes revenue.

data.title: TechCreate Group Ltd. Reports First Half Fiscal Year 2026 Financial and Operational Results
data.description:
TechCreate Group Ltd. (OTCMKTS: TCGLF) (“TechCreate” or the “Company”), a technology consultancy and advanced software solutions provider specializing in payment solutions, cybersecurity, and digital services, announced its financial and operational results for the six months ended June 30, 2026.

Recent Operational Highlights

  • Notified by NYSE American that the Committee for Review will consider the Company’s request for review of the Panel’s decision on October 22, 2026

  • Issued a Letter to Shareholders explaining NYSE American delisting proceedings

  • Announced changes to the Board of Directors and committee composition, effective May 31, 2026

  • Announced intention to collaborate with pQCee Pte Ltd to explore the incorporation of National Institute of Standards and Technology-approved post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithms in the Company’s QR Hybrid POS terminals

  • Appointed Sibil Thomas as Financial Controller and Chief Accounting Officer

First Half Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results

Total Revenues decreased to approximately S$880,000 (US$680,000) for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to S$1.9 million in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily due to lower Provision of Professional Services revenue, reflecting the completion in 2025 of a Real-Time Engine enhancement project for a customer in Brunei and an OEM pay enablement project for a customer in Cambodia, lower Sale of Software Licenses and Maintenance Licenses revenue following the expiration of existing contracts with customers in Cambodia and Brunei, and lower Sale of Hardware Solutions revenue mainly attributable to lower sales of QR soundbox terminals during the first half of 2026.

Cost of Revenue decreased to approximately S$579,000 (US$447,000) for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to S$890,000 in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily due to lower costs associated with the decrease in revenue.

Gross Profit Margin decreased to 34.2% for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to 54.0% in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily due to lower revenue from Provision of Professional Services.

Total Operating Expenses increased to S$2.6 million (US$2.0 million) for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to S$1.0 million in the same period last year. The increase was primarily due to an increase in general and administrative expenses reflecting higher professional fees associated with the Company’s post-IPO strategic initiatives and an increase in selling and distribution expenses reflecting higher staff costs associated with the expansion of the Company’s sales team.

Net Loss was S$2.2 million (US$1.7 million) for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of approximately S$20,000 in the same period last year. The increase was primarily due to the decrease in revenue and the increase in operating expenses, partially offset by higher other income and lower interest expense.

As of June 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were approximately S$6.5 million (US$5.1 million), compared to S$7.4 million as of December 31, 2025.

Management Commentary

TechCreate CEO Heng Hai Lim commented: “Our first half results reflect the completion in 2025 of two large projects in Brunei and Cambodia and the expiration of several software license contracts that were not replaced within the period, while operating expenses increased primarily due to professional fees associated with our post-IPO initiatives. The suspension of trading in our shares and the ongoing NYSE American delisting proceeds have also affected our planned U.S. expansion and related revenue opportunities. That said, we ended the period with approximately S$6.5 million in cash, which we believe gives us the resources to keep investing as we rebuild our revenue base. Looking ahead, we are focused on converting our pipeline into contracted revenue and broadening our offerings. During the first half, we began investing in research and development, including our collaboration with pQCee on post-quantum cryptography for our QR Hybrid POS Terminal, and we expanded our sales team to extend our market reach. We believe real-time payments, quantum-safe security, and AI within our Real-Time Engine represent meaningful opportunities for the Company.

“We recognize that our listing status remains top of mind for shareholders. We have appealed the Listing Qualifications Panel’s decision to the NYSE Committee for Review, which is scheduled to consider the matter on October 22, 2026. Neither the Panel nor NYSE American has found that the Company engaged in any wrongdoing, and no regulator has charged the Company or any of its directors, officers, or employees in connection with the trading activity that led to the suspension. Our goal is to relist on NYSE American, although we cannot assure that the Committee will reverse the Panel’s decision. In the meantime, we remain laser focused on growing the underlying business. We sincerely appreciate our shareholders’ continued patience and support as the Committee considers our appeal.”

About TechCreate Group Ltd.

TechCreate Group Ltd. is a Singapore-based payment software solutions provider. Founded in 2015, the Company delivers digital payment and infrastructure solutions to financial institutions, telecommunications, deposit insurance, and enterprises. TechCreate’s offerings include real-time payment systems, digital banking platforms, API management, cybersecurity, and cloud computing. Its proprietary Artificial Intelligence Real-Time Engine (AI-RTE) is designed to enable fast, secure, and efficient payment processing. For more information, visit https://www.techcreate.com.sg/.

data.title: Cisco Stocks Rise Higher as Webex Gives AI Agents Shared Context
data.description:
Cisco, the networking, security and collaboration provider , introduced new Webex AI capabilities, with shares at $116.34, up approximately 1.26% from the previous close, around 10:35 a.m. ET on October 9. The pitch goes beyond meeting summaries: give agents permission to use company information and tackle tasks across applications. The valuation picture raises the bar, showing shares 54.75% above the $75.18 GF Value estimate.

Cisco says Claude Managed Agents will bring analysis and coordinated actions into Webex, while an OpenAI dots integration will feed meeting and team information into personal agents. Its announcement also outlines Dialog, which lets customer-service agents keep working after a conversation finishes, and puts RoomOS 27 availability in November. The release provides no pricing or paid-adoption figures. More capability is coming. The revenue proof still needs to follow.

The potential payoff reaches beyond Webex subscriptions. Cisco could sell the identity controls, AI Defense protection and Splunk monitoring that businesses need when agents start taking action. That gives the company a plausible route to larger customer contracts. But the valuation premium leaves little room for a rollout that adds features without adding spending. Investors need evidence that customers will pay for the broader packageand that those sales will lift earnings.

data.title: CJP October 10 Delhi protest news: Internet to be suspended in 4-km radius of Janpath-Kartvya Path starting 10 pm Friday
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 9 -- Internet services in central Delhi will remain suspended at and around a radiums of 4 km from Janpath-Kartvya Path Cross from 10 pm on Friday, 9 October to 10 pm on Saturday, 10th October, Delhi Police's Deputy Commissioner Manishi Chandra said in a letter to the nodal officials of telecom companies Airtel, Vodafone-Idea, Jio, and MTNL.

The letter mentions that the request was sent to the Union Home Secretary, who has considered the same.

This move comes ahead of the planned protest by the Cockroach Janta Party and other student organisations at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Saturday to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the rollback of the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

A number of steps have been taken by the government ahead of the protest, including closing of 57 Delhi Metro stations, stopping a number of long-distance training that were going to Delhi.

Thousands of police and paramilitary forces were being sent into the national capital for the protest, Reuters reported citing a government document.

The Supreme Court on Friday objected to restrictions imposed in Delhi ahead of the October 10 protests that could disrupt the normal lives of citizens, particularly those who have no intention of joining the ongoing demonstrations.

A bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also clarified that the present proceedings primarily concern restrictions affecting the movement of ordinary citizens and public transport and not the broader right to protest.

"We have serious concerns about this. Our concern is not about the protesters, or about the authorities, but about hundreds and thousands of commuters in Delhi for their livelihood, children and senior citizens. We are talking about common citizenry. They should not be disturbed. Everybody doesn't have a car or facilities," the CJI said.

Alcohol shops also remained closed on Friday in Delhi and will continue to remain so on on Saturday.

A traders' organisation in Delhi's Connaught Place has asked their members to keep their shops closed on Saturday in order to avoid any untoward incident.

data.title: Netflix Is Getting Leaner Again
data.description:
Netflix Inc. (NFLX, Financials), the streaming entertainment giant, is apparently looking to eliminate around 5% of its personnel in an effort to run more effectively in an increasingly competitive media industry.

Citing persons familiar with the subject, the newspaper said an announcement may come as soon as next week. There was no comment from Netflix.

The corporation employed around 16,000 full-time employees at the end of last year. So, a 5% cut would amount to around 800 jobs if spread evenly throughout that workforce.

The projected cuts would be significant for a firm that last made large layoffs in 2022 when Netflix slashed hundreds of jobs as membership growth slowed. This time it's a whole different story.

Rather than withdrawing from growth, Netflix has been moving into new areas beyond its core subscription model. It is counting on advertising, live programming and games to find other sources of revenue.

At the same time, it's becoming more difficult to fight for attention. Media consolidation is changing the streaming business, and YouTube is grabbing a larger bite of viewing time and ad dollars.

This makes the rumored layoffs as much a story about efficiency as it is about cost-cutting. Investors will want to see if Netflix can cut costs without damaging newer growth efforts.

The next catalyst will be a formal statement possibly as soon as next week on the scope and regions of the reduction.

data.title: US energy firms add rigs for fourth time in five weeks to highest since 2024, Baker Hughes says
data.description:
By Scott DiSavino

US energy firms this week added rigs for the fourth time in five weeks, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, rose by five to 603 in the week to October 9, its highest since May 2024. (BHGUSWTT), (BHGUSOILDRLW), (BHGUSGASDRLW) (USOIRC=ECI), (USGSRC=ECI)

Baker Hughes said this week's increase put the total rig count up 56 rigs, or 10% above this time last year.

Baker Hughes said oil rigs rose by six to 462 this week, their highest since May 2025, while gas rigs fell by one to 132, their lowest since mid-September, and other miscellaneous rigs held at nine.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower US oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than on increasing output.

But now spot US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude prices are expected to rise in 2026 for the first time in four years due to supply disruptions from the Iran war. The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) projected that crude output will rise from a record 13.7 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025 to 13.9 million bpd in 2026.

On the gas side, EIA projected that output will jump from a record 107.6 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 112.2 bcfd in 2026 as demand for the fuel rises to produce electricity for power-hungry data centers and liquefied natural gas (LNG) for export.

data.title: Capital Concentration Amplifies BDC Woes, Credit Executives Say — WSJ
data.description:
By Isaac Taylor

Private-credit executives point to an overreliance on a small group of wirehouse brokers and wealth management gatekeepers as a primary driver behind surging withdrawal requests from nontraded business-development companies over the past year or so.

These wealth advisers, including some within banks, funneled capital from individual investors into BDCs over the past few years, a trend that fueled the spate of elevated shareholder redemptions, according to several attendees of this year's Greenwich Economic Forum.

Over the past few years, direct lenders like Blue Owl Capital and KKR channeled wealthy investors into their BDCs, touting their double-digit yields, according to industry executives speaking on the conference sidelines earlier this week.

But much of that money arrived through a pipeline of banks, brokers and wealth advisers such as Morgan Stanley, UBS and Bank of America's Merrill unit. None of the advisers, brokers or banks responded to requests for comment.

Some of the credit firms that have been affected more significantly than others by the withdrawals received billions of dollars through these channels, said Ken Kencel, the president and chief executive of Churchill Asset Management.

"When those firms turn, it can be a massive turn," he added, speaking on one of the forum panels.

Across the roughly $2 trillion private-credit industry, a widening divide has emerged over the past year between funds fulfilling quarterly redemptions smoothly and those forced to ration client cash behind customary 5% withdrawal limits.

While signs of stress in private credit persist, the market hasn't collapsed. Payment-in-kind income reported by BDCs has remained elevated at about 8% in recent quarters, according to a September report from credit evaluator Fitch Ratings.

Redemptions also remained elevated, although all 19 of the vehicles tracked by Fitch capped redemptions at 5% of net asset value in this year's second quarter, and net capital flows remained negative compared with the preceding quarter, Fitch said.

Publicly traded BDCs and funds have fallen from their peak last year and trade around 82% of their NAVs following this year's uncertainty. Ares Capital Corp. shares have declined 7.1% this year, while FS KKR Capital has plunged 27% and Blue Owl Capital Corp. has dropped 18%.

Public scrutiny has largely focused on credit trouble related to some private equity-backed software companies whose businesses may be threatened by artificial intelligence advances. But several Greenwich forum participants said from the sidelines that the real fault lies in the plumbing that sent much of the money to the BDCs in the first place.

The executives said much of it is the byproduct of risks created by the reliance on a few wirehouses and wealth advisers for capital.

When just one of these conduits decides to trim its target allocation to private debt, the decision ripples across potentially thousands of advisers and client accounts. That can translate into exit orders amounting to billions of dollars hitting a single BDC overnight.

This change in distribution priorities can trigger even more redemption requests and create a run-like dynamic even without any deterioration in the quality of an evergreen fund's or BDC's underlying credit holdings.

Ways to avoid this concentration risk include anchoring funds with institutional capital and improving investor understanding of terms such as semi-liquid, executives at the forum said. An institutional anchor investor or two can prevent a single broker or bank from flooding quarterly liquidity windows and triggering runs, they said.

And they stressed finding ways to ensure that investors who enter these pools through retail channels understand what they are getting. Credit funds need to make sure that wealthy investors know that their cash won't be returned under some circumstances, Kencel said, following his panel appearance.

"I think the lesson has been learned," he said. "When you think about the marketing of some of these private-credit funds, they were called semi-liquid."

Write to Isaac Taylor at isaac.taylor@wsj.com

data.title: S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq Rise After Steep AI Sell-Off
data.description:
U.S. equities edged higher Friday as buyers returned to the market following a technology-led pullback in the previous session. The S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average and Nasdaq Composite each gained about 0.4% in morning trading.

Gains extended beyond technology, with eight of the S&P 500's 11 sectors trading higher. Consumer discretionary and real estate shares led the advance, while industrial stocks lagged, pointing to a broader recovery rather than a rally confined to AI-related companies.

Recent pressure on technology stocks followed concerns about OpenAI's revenue trajectory. Reports put the company's annualized revenue at $50 billion at the end of September, below the $68 billion figure reported a month earlier. The figures added to investor scrutiny of whether spending on artificial intelligence will translate into the growth expected by markets.

Economic data offered another concern. The preliminary October reading of consumer sentiment fell more than economists anticipated, while inflation expectations increased. That combination could complicate the outlook for household spending and the Federal Reserve's policy path, leaving investors to weigh the market rebound against persistent uncertainty over AI monetization and inflation.

data.title: Center says no monopoly in satcom; Starlink among 3 licensed operators awaiting next steps
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 9 -- A high-stakes showdown over satellite internet rollout in India has erupted, pitting SpaceX CEO Elon Musk against the Indian government and domestic telecom majors, and spiralling into a political clash involving the Opposition.

At the centre is the delay in granting commercial approval to Starlink. The government response came at the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC 2026) in the national capital, where Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia rejected allegations of preferential treatment or cronyism in the satcom licensing process.

Addressing queries at IMC 2026, Scindia said India will not allow a monopoly in any sector. He said three players have received licences and are operating on a level playing field.

"Let me be very clear. India does not allow a monopoly in any sector. And therefore, even as Satcom is concerned, there is not a single licensee that has been chosen. Licences have been given to everyone who wants to provide these licences. And today three licences are out there," Scindia said.

The three licensed Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite (GMPCS) operators are Reliance Jio Satcom, Bharti Airtel-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Starlink. Scindia added that Amazon's Project Kuiper has also expressed interest and will have to undergo standard evaluation.

Scindia outlined a three-stage roadmap. Spectrum allocation policy, the decision to assign satellite spectrum administratively rather than through auction has been finalised. Pricing regime, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) are finalising spectrum pricing and revenue-sharing and security clearance assessments by the Ministry of Home Affairs and national security agencies are underway.

"Initially, whether spectrum will be assigned or auctioned, that decision was taken. Secondly, irrespective of administrative assignment, what the pricing regime will be. And TRAI and DoT have been in conversations on that. We are close to taking the final decision with respect to that. And the third has to do with security requirements and requisites being followed," Scindia said.

"Once the revenue charges system is finalised, once each one of these parties, party A, B, and C, all three, individually based on their achievement of milestones with regard to security concerns and prerequisites, have fulfilled the requirements, then obviously they can start operations," he added.

The timeline triggered public remarks from Elon Musk. On X, Musk wrote: "Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license?"

Musk alleged that corporate interests were blocking Starlink: "Unfortunately, we (Starlink) are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are . This is a crime against the people of India."

He then named Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani, asking, "Is Ambani the real boss of India?" Musk argued the delay hurts rural India, which lacks high-speed connectivity, while urban users already have robust access.

The Ministry of Communications and Minister of State for Communications Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani dismissed Musk's charges as "baseless and misconceived," saying provisional spectrum and licences are held equally by all three players while final security clearances from the MHA remain pending for all.

Security requirements flagged include data localisation, ensuring Indian user data stays within borders, and ground terminal security to mitigate dual-use risks and regulate foreign Low-Earth Orbit access.

Addressing this at IMC 2026 on October 7, Lauren Dreyer, Vice President of Starlink Business Operations at SpaceX, said: "We are keeping Indian users' data within India."Dreyer said Starlink has established 20 gateway sites in India, developed India-specific security controls, and is "standing ready to serve India once India is ready."

The row turned political after Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi replied to Musk's post, "Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy."

Musk responded, "Thank you, Rahul. This is indeed troubling."

The BJP hit back at Gandhi for siding with a foreign billionaire against domestic security protocols, saying clearances cannot be bypassed for corporate schedules.

Scindia also criticised the Congress's stance, "And as far as the Congress party is concerned, I don't understand. I don't think they themselves know whether they're going left or right. They first had a problem initially with a certain person getting a licence. Now they have a problem, and they've allied with that person in terms of why he's not getting a licence."

At a CEO roundtable during IMC 2026, Scindia reiterated, "The government is technology agnostic. Our job is to provide a bouquet of services. It is for customers to choose in a free market what they prefer."

Licensing is completed for Starlink, Reliance Jio Satcom and Eutelsat OneWeb. The allocation methodology, administrative assignment over auction, is completed. Pricing and revenue sharing are near completion, with DoT and TRAI finalising the framework.

Security clearance is underway, with MHA evaluating data localisation, gateway access and terminal security. Commercial launch remains pending, dependent on each operator individually fulfilling security requirements.

data.title: Tesla Stock Jumps as Shanghai Deliveries Rise for 11th Straight Month
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) shares climbed 3% in morning trading Friday after fresh data showed higher sales of electric vehicles manufactured in China, while demand in Europe continued to recover.

The company delivered 95,366 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles produced at its Shanghai factory in September, a 5% increase from 90,812 units a year earlier, according to China Passenger Car Association data released Friday. The latest increase extended the annual growth streak to 11 months.

Shanghai-built vehicle sales also advanced 13.7% year over year in the third quarter. However, Tesla's worldwide deliveries fell 2.1% from the same period last year, when the automaker recorded a quarterly delivery record. Global deliveries nevertheless exceeded analysts' expectations.

Tesla is offering discounts in China through October to support demand amid intensifying competition. Selected Model Y versions qualify for a 7,000-yuan discount on final payments, while Model 3 buyers can receive 5,000 yuan off.

Investors will watch whether stronger regional sales can translate into sustained worldwide delivery growth as Tesla navigates pricing pressure and competition in the electric vehicle market.

data.title: US consumer spending remained solid in September, BofA says
data.description:
Key points:
  • Main US equity indexes modestly higher
  • Real estate leads S&P 500 sector gainers; Communication Services is sole loser
  • Dollar gains; gold, bitcoin both up >1%; US crude edges higher
  • US 10-year Treasury yield edges up to ~5.25%

US CONSUMER SPENDING REMAINED SOLID IN SEPTEMBER, BOFA SAYS

US consumer spending remained robust in September, with lower- and middle-income households joining high earners in driving demand, according to a report from Bank of America Institute.

Aggregate credit and debit card spending per household rose 6.2% from a year earlier in September, or 5.1% excluding gasoline purchases, marking the third-strongest annual growth rate of the past four years, the report said.

Retail spending excluding gasoline increased 3.5%, while services spending climbed 5.4%, with most discretionary retail categories posting gains.

Spending among lower-income households stood at 5.5% in September, outpacing growth among middle-income households at 4.9% and higher-income households at 4.8%. Only the top 5% of earners spent at a faster pace, with spending growth of 5.9%, according to the report.

Spending on holiday-related items in September was running ahead of comparable periods in 2025, though some of the increase may be attributable to higher prices rather than stronger purchase volumes.

One area under scrutiny ahead of the holidays is the use of buy-now, pay-later financing. Bank of America said 8.3% of households in its deposit data made a BNPL payment in September, with usage continuing to rise gradually but showing no signs of a sharp acceleration.

"Overall, in our view, the increase in the share of BNPL users heading into the season does not appear too concerning, though the rate of usage for some BNPL consumers does bear watching," the report said.

data.title: USDA WASDE Report Sparks Liquidation Rush in Corn Futures — Update
data.description:
By Kirk Maltais

The Agriculture Department lifted its projections for the size of this year's corn crop, sparking traders to accelerate the liquidation of their sizable long holdings.

The USDA forecast corn production would be at its second-highest level ever, at 16.03 billion bushels, in the 2026/27 marketing year, behind last year's 17 billion bushels of corn produced, in its monthly World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates report published Friday.

Average yields are anticipated at 181.2 bushels an acre, a 2.7 bushels-an-acre increase from the USDA's September estimate. Analysts surveyed by The Wall Street Journal forecast yield this month at 177.6 bushels an acre, a 0.9 bushels-an-acre decline from last month.

Most-active corn futures trading on the Chicago Board of Trade plummeted after the USDA released its updated projections, falling 5.1% to $4.89 a bushel - retreating under the $5 a bushel mark.

The larger corn crop, combined with last month's quarterly stock report showing larger-than-expected inventories of corn, has the market rethinking its assumptions about the weather stress seen in the latter-half of the summer and its effect on crop health.

"Sept. 1 stocks coming in 173 million bushels above the September WASDE pretty much guaranteed ending stocks would climb," said Brian Grete, senior grain and livestock analyst with Commstock Investments. "But not this much, because a smaller crop was anticipated."

Fund traders were largely expecting a shrinking corn crop this year, with last week's Commitment of Traders report from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission showing a net long position of 377,850 contracts among managed money. The agency will be publishing an updated version of the report later Friday afternoon.

For soybeans, the USDA affirmed its estimates for record-large production and yields for the 2026/27 crop. The USDA said 4.56 billion bushels of soybeans would be harvested in the U.S. this fall, boasting an average yield of 53.1 bushels an acre. Both figures are record-highs for U.S. soybeans, with the previous record for production set at 4.46 billion bushels in 2021 and yields at 53 bushels an acre in 2025.

Friday's move in soybeans was largely expected by analysts, but the surprise factor in corn has diverted attention away from soybeans and wheat.

"The numbers couldn't get much worse for the corn," Charlie Sernatinger, executive vice president with Marex Capital Markets, said in a note following the WASDE's release. "The beans were 'neutral,' but nothing is neutral when the grain locomotive takes off in a new direction."

Most-active soybean futures are down 0.9%, while wheat has fallen 2.6%.

Write to Kirk Maltais at kirk.maltais@wsj.com

data.title: Lakshmi Venu pushes for settlement along lines of TVS family partition
data.description:
To settle the dispute over wealth sharing within the Venu Srinivasan family, Lakshmi Venu, daughter of Venu Srinivasan and Mallika Srinivasan, is understood to be pushing for a settlement along the lines of the broader TVS family partition in 2020.

Sudarshan Venu

Sources close to Lakshmi said that the harmonious partition and settlement between four major wings of the TVS family can be a model to settle the wealth of the Venu Srinivasan group comprising of TVS Motor, Sundaram Clayton, TVS Holdings, and TVS Credit.

In 2020, the larger TVS family comprising multiple branches valued all assets, divided them on a mutually agreeable basis and also compensated family members.

However, this demand has led to an impasse.

According to insiders, Venu Srinivasan and Sudarshan have shown resistance to a formal settlement. “Multiple requests by Lakshmi Venu to her father and brother, Sudarshan, over the last several months have been met with silence,” said a person close to the family. The father-son duo is understood to be of the view that a family settlement was already executed via a 2024 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by all four members.

However, this particular MoU, reviewed by businessline, does not speak of any financial settlement and just lays down details of brand rights and non-compete arrangements.

As per the document, Venu and Sudarshan control automobiles, financial services, real estate and drone business of TVS Holdings, and Venu and Lakshmi control Sundaram-Clayton. Mallika and Lakshmi manage TAFE, which is not part of the TVS group.

The dispute started when Lakshmi came to know of a TVS Holdings statutory filing in April 2025 declaring significant beneficial ownership in favour of Sudarshan Venu.

“Lakshmi was shocked as family wealth cannot be allocated unilaterally without discussion,” the source said. She is not taking legal action yet and continues to try and address this internally, the person added.

businessline has also learnt that Mallika Srinivasan, as the mother of Lakshmi and Sudarshan, is attempting to get the family together for a dialogue and believes that it could be settled within. “She wants this issue to end with a fair and equitable settlement and is in favour of getting a neutral mediator for the purpose ​,” a close family source said, adding that there should be no gender disparity in sharing of the family wealth.

The source emphasised that the issue is not just about economic settlement between family members but about ownership and management of the group companies. “Someone who has managed the company, even if he did well, cannot claim ownership over it,” the source said.

Mallika is said to have taken a strong view that a person creating value in the company does not automatically extinguish legal ownership rights of the other.

As of Friday, TVS Holdings had a market cap of ₹23,180 crore, TVS Motor is valued at ₹1,83,621 crore and Sundaram Clayton at around ₹2,702 crore.

data.title: Canadian dollar hits 18-month low as jobs data clips rate hike bets
data.description:
By Fergal Smith

The Canadian dollar weakened to an 18-month low against its US counterpart on Friday as domestic data showed a surprise drop in employment, reducing expectations for a Bank of Canada interest rate hike this month.

The loonie was trading 0.4% lower at 1.4275 per US dollar, or 70.05 US cents, after touching its weakest intraday level since April 2025 at 1.4298. For the week, the currency was down 0.2%, putting it on track for its fifth straight weekly decline.

  • Canada's economy shed 68,300 jobs in September, while the unemployment rate edged up to 6.5% from 6.4% in August. Economists had forecast an increase of 9,200 jobs.

  • "A second consecutive month of sizable job losses washes away the surprising strength reported in Canada's job market through the early summer, and leaves employment up a so-so 0.5% from a year ago," Douglas Porter, chief economist at BMO Capital Markets, said in a note.

  • "We continue to believe that the appropriate stance by the Bank of Canada is watchful waiting, particularly so with employment suddenly clouding over," Porter said.

  • The BoC has said it is prepared to raise borrowing costs multiple times if inflation remained too high but it has also worried that new US tariffs had increased uncertainty around the sustainability of Canada's economic rebound.

  • Investors see a 25% chance the central bank raises its benchmark interest rate on October 28, down from 40% before the employment report. (0#CADIRPR)

  • The US dollar rose against a basket of major currencies as oil prices recovered from session lows. US crude oil futures were trading 0.3% lower at $91.19 a barrel.

  • Canadian government bond yields moved lower across the curve, with the market set to close early ahead of the Thanksgiving Day holiday on Monday.

  • The 2-year (CA2YT=RR) was down 6.8 basis points at 3.183%, falling 10.9 basis points further below the equivalent US rate to a gap of about 161 basis points, its widest since February 2025.
